scope: Manual selected shipped-source lifecycle review with catalog public declaration checks. Not a separate stable documented mod contract or whole-game source/binary equivalence.
findings: RoomInstance.remove checks existence and tile membership, deactivates/disposes, removes blueprint registration, then transfers geometry into the singleton TmpArea and clears the old indexed room slot.
RoomsMap.create chooses a free indexed slot using lastIndex and can reuse a removed ID. Loaded saves can contain earlier free slots, so the first replacement need not reuse the removed ID.
RoomBlueprintIns.removeInstance uses ArrayListResize.removeOrdered: later warehouse discovery slots shift left after removal. This static finding is not a multi-room native acceptance case.

Furnisher.create dispatches the warehouse construction implementation; StockpileInstance consumes existing furnishing cells, builds crate bookkeeping, can pick up scattered resources, then activates. A public zero-default RoomInit is fixture input, not a faithful material-cost simulation.
TmpArea must be consumed or cleared within the same callback. The fixture does not retain it across callbacks or publish it through MCP.
Public finished-room statistics are adjusted after test reconstruction to pair with the next public removal. No normal save or production mutation path is added.
limits: Actual compiler access and MCP lifecycle outcomes are reported separately in STOCKPILE_LIFECYCLE_VALIDATION.json.
Internal implementation methods are inspected statically only, never called reflectively or accessed as private runtime fields.
No source text, game archive, state rows or copied save is redistributed.
